arxiv-2101-10564.title: The ergodic Mean Field Game system for a type of state constraint condition
arxiv-2101-10564.creator: Mariya Sardarli
arxiv-2101-10564.description: Abstract 1 Introduction The object of this paper is to establish well-posedness (existence and uniqueness) results for a type of state constraint ergodic Mean Field Game (MFG) system \displaystyle\begin{cases}-\Delta u+H(Du)+\rho=F(x;m)&\text{ in }\Omega,\\ \Delta m+div(mD_{p}H(Du))=0&\text{ in }\Omega,\\ m\geq 0,\quad\int_{\Omega}m=1,\end{cases} (1.1) supplemented with the state constraint-type infinite Dirichlet boundary condition \lim\limits_{d(x)\to 0}u(x)=\infty, (1.2) where d(x):=d(x,\partial\Omega) is the distance to the boundary.

arxiv-2102-11814.title: A Multi-Stage Stochastic Programming Approach to Epidemic Resource Allocation with Equity Considerations Thanks: Cite as: Yin, X. and Büyüktahtakın İ. E., 2021. A multi-stage stochastic programming approach to epidemic resource allocation with equity considerations. Health Care Management Science, p
arxiv-2102-11814.creator: Xuecheng Yin, İ. Esra Büyüktahtakın
arxiv-2102-11814.description: Abstract Existing compartmental models in epidemiology are limited in terms of optimizing the resource allocation to control an epidemic outbreak under disease growth uncertainty. In this study, we address this core limitation by presenting a multi-stage stochastic programming compartmental model, which integrates the uncertain disease progression and resource allocation to control an infectious disease outbreak.

arxiv-2203-05798.title: On the p p -torsion of the Tate-Shafarevich group of abelian varieties over higher dimensional bases over finite fields Thanks: I thank Jean-Louis Colliot-Thélène, Aise Johan de Jong, Ulrich Görtz, Uwe Jannsen and Moritz Kerz, and Ariyan Javanpeykar, darx and David Loeffler from mathoverflow. I also
arxiv-2203-05798.creator: Timo Keller
arxiv-2203-05798.description: Abstract . We prove a finiteness theorem for the first flat cohomology group of finite flat group schemes over integral normal proper varieties over finite fields. As a consequence, we can prove the invariance of the finiteness of the Tate-Shafarevich group of Abelian schemes over higher dimensional bases under isogenies and alterations over/of such bases for the p p -part.

arxiv-2206-00257.title: CoNSoLe : Convex Neural Symbolic Learning
arxiv-2206-00257.creator: Haoran Li, Yang Weng, Hanghang Tong
arxiv-2206-00257.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Haoran Li, Yang Weng, Hanghang Tong. Learning the underlying equation from data is a fundamental problem in many disciplines. Recent advances rely on Neural Networks (NNs) but do not provide theoretical guarantees in obtaining the exact equations owing to the non-convexity of NNs. In this paper, we propose Co nvex N eural S ymb o lic Le arning ( CoNSoLe ) to seek convexity under mild conditions. The main idea is to decompose the recovering process into two steps and convexify each step.

arxiv-2211-08598.title: Compatible Director Fields in ℝ 3 \mathbb{R}^{3}
arxiv-2211-08598.creator: Luiz C. B. da Silva, Tal Bar, Efi Efrati
arxiv-2211-08598.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Luiz C. B. da Silva, Tal Bar, Efi Efrati. The geometry and interactions between the constituents of a liquid crystal, which are responsible for inducing the partial order in the fluid, may locally favor an attempted phase that could not be realized in ℝ 3 \mathbb{R}^{3} . While states that are incompatible with the geometry of ℝ 3 \mathbb{R}^{3} were identified more than 50 years ago, the collection of compatible states remained poorly understood and not well characterized.

arxiv-2410-21105.title: Difference-in-Differences with Time-varying Continuous Treatments Using Double/Debiased Machine Learning Thanks: We gratefully acknowledge comments from Michael Knaus and participants at the Valais Econometrics Workshop 2025. Addresses for correspondence: Michel F. C. Haddad, Bancroft Building, Quee
arxiv-2410-21105.creator: Michel F. C. Haddad
arxiv-2410-21105.description: Abstract We propose a difference-in-differences (DiD) framework designed for time-varying continuous treatments across multiple periods. Specifically, we estimate the average treatment effect on the treated (ATET) by comparing distinct non-zero treatment intensities. Identification rests on a conditional parallel trends assumption that accounts for observed covariates and past treatment histories.

arxiv-2503-00659.creator: Namo Asavisanu, Tina Khezresmaeilzadeh, Rohan Sequeira, Hang Qiu
arxiv-2503-00659.description: Abstract With cooperative perception, autonomous vehicles can wirelessly share sensor data and representations to overcome sensor occlusions, improving situational awareness. Securing such data exchanges is crucial for connected autonomous vehicles. Existing, automated reputation-based approaches often suffer from a delay between detection and exclusion of misbehaving vehicles, while majority-based approaches have communication overheads that limits scalability.

arxiv-2510-10867.title: Explicitly Computing with Fukaya Categories of Surfaces with Boundary
arxiv-2510-10867.creator: Chris Grossack
arxiv-2510-10867.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Chris Grossack. Fukaya categories are deep and rich invariants of symplectic manifolds which are notoriously difficult to compute explicitly. In the case of surfaces, however, the situation is simple, combinatorial, and is very well understood (at least by experts). In this expository paper we will give an introduction with many examples to welcome newcomers to the area and hopefully equip them with the tools to independently compute Fukaya categories of surfaces.

pmc-10638014.title: A new optical pH sensor based on a mixture of Alizarin and Orange dyes immobilized on an agarose membrane
pmc-10638014.creator: Kamal Alizadeh, Behrooz Rezaei, Hadi Nemati
pmc-10638014.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Two techniques, including chemical immobilization of a combination of two indicators of Alizarin and Orange dyes and the epoxy activation of the agarose membrane, were used for the preparation of a new optic pH sensor. pmc-10642161.creator: Arslan Habib, Yulai Liang, Naishuo Zhu

pmc-12603043.title: Long-term forecasting of the impact of EV home charging at different adoption rates on the Egyptian load profile
pmc-12603043.creator: David Salah Roushdy Beshay, Mohamed Abdul Raouf Shafei, Doaa Khalil Ibrahim
pmc-12603043.description: Predicting the impact of electric vehicle (EV) fleet charging load on the grid load profile is essential for policymakers during grid planning. A systematic three-stage framework is proposed to forecast the long-term impact of EV home charging on national grids.

pmc-12836935.creator: Penghui Li, Yuan Xue, Xinyu Gu
pmc-12836935.description: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are instrumental in the progression and regulation of gastric cancer (GC), affecting various cellular processes including gene expression, apoptosis, cell proliferation, and metastasis. N6-methyladenosine (m6A), a dynamic and reversible RNA modification, profoundly influences GC by modulating RNA metabolism and function, impacting RNA stability, maturation, and interactions.

uslaw-usc-t38-s3540.title: 38 U.S.C. § 3540 — Purpose
uslaw-usc-t38-s3540.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t38-s3540.description: United States Code, Title 38 (Veterans’ Benefits); Part III (Readjustment And Related Benefits); Chapter 35 (Survivors’ And Dependents’ Educational Assistance); Subchapter V (Special Restorative Training). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The purpose of special restorative training is to overcome, or lessen, the effects of a manifest physical or mental disability which would handicap an eligible person (other than a person made eligible.
